newsitem.title: UK: Midlands Elec eyes gas competition.
newsitem.headline: Midlands Elec eyes gas competition.

text.p: Avon Energy's Midlands Electricity said its subsidiary Midlands Gas Ltd planned to enter the second phase of Britain's domestic gas market competition.
The second phase will expand existing trials in south west England to southern England and should kick off early next year.
First phase trials are already underway covering some 500,000 domestic gas users in the south west of the country.
The second phase will cover 1.5 million users, raising the total number of users trying out competition in the market to two million, a spokesman for industry watchdog Ofgas said.
Ofgas is expected to issue a consultation document on the second phase of competition by mid-September.
Midlands Gas Ltd did not take part in the first round of trials, where nine companies are competing with the privatised British Gas Plc.

Midlands will have to apply to Ofgas for a licence to participate in the second phase, the Ofgas spokesman said. Britain's gas market to domestic users is due to be liberalised fully sometime in 1998.
